head: d7505672f3bd902490d6625712e1eb0f9b863bc2
claim: an app can run two bots as two Pi processes on two sessions, each answering from its own AGENTS.md, with the person's Pi folder unchanged

steps.start: Worktree at commit d7505672 with npm dependencies installed and the workspace built (npm run build exited 0). Scratch HOME was an empty folder, so ~/.pi was a stand-in folder holding one canary AGENTS.md and an auth.json.
steps: Read the done-done verify skill and the pi-bots feature recipe.
Ran npm run build in the worktree; it exited 0.
Wrote a node consumer that imports the built @byokit/pi entry, starts a loopback stand-in model server, and creates two bot folders (chief and scout), each with its own AGENTS.md.
Ran the consumer with HOME set to an empty folder; it created two bots from one kit, sent 'hello chief' and 'hello scout' at the same time, and waited for both replies.
Checked each bot's model call: each carried its own AGENTS.md text and not the parent canary; each bot had one session file.
Sent 'hold' to chief, then steered it with 'turn left' while the answer was in progress; read the steered reply.
Sent 'hold' to chief again and aborted it; read the abort result.
Waited for scout to go idle, checked that its process was gone, sent 'still there', and read which messages the model saw.
Closed the kit and the stand-in server, tried to create a kit on the person's Pi folder, and compared the folder's hash before and after the run.
steps.result: The console shows two bots with different process ids answering 'heard: hello chief' and 'heard: hello scout'; each bot's own AGENTS.md is in its context and the parent canary is not. The steer reply is 'heard: turn left', the abort result is { ok: false, aborted: true }, scout stopped idle with its process gone, and its next model call saw 'hello scout' and 'still there'. The person's Pi folder was refused with code person-pi and its hash was the same after the run.

verdicts.seen: I read all 9 entries. The capture states "two-bots pids differ: true", shows both "heard: hello chief" and "heard: hello scout", and reports for chief and scout "own context true", "any canary false", and "session files 1". It also reports "person-pi same hash: true", supporting that the person's Pi folder was unchanged. The steer-abort and idle-resume lines do not contradict the outcome.
